title: Phrenic Nerve Anatomy
text: The phrenic nerve originates from cervical spinal cord levels C3, C4, and C5. It is the sole motor supply to the diaphragm and also provides sensory innervation to the central diaphragm, pericardium, and mediastinal pleura.

title: Metformin Mechanism of Action
text: Metformin is a biguanide that acts primarily by inhibiting hepatic gluconeogenesis via activation of AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK). It is the first-line pharmacological treatment for type 2 diabetes mellitus according to international guidelines.

title: Methotrexate Drug Interactions
text: Concomitant use of methotrexate with trimethoprim significantly increases the risk of severe bone marrow suppression due to additive antifolate effects. This combination should be avoided. If unavoidable, close haematological monitoring is mandatory.

title: Aspirin Pharmacology
text: Aspirin (acetylsalicylic acid) irreversibly inhibits both cyclooxygenase-1 (COX-1) and cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) enzymes by acetylating a serine residue. This prevents the synthesis of thromboxane A2 and prostaglandins.

title: Warfarin and Antibiotic Interactions
text: Fluoroquinolone antibiotics including ciprofloxacin can significantly increase the anticoagulant effect of warfarin by inhibiting CYP1A2 and reducing vitamin K-producing gut flora. INR should be monitored closely when ciprofloxacin is co-prescribed with warfarin.
